fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.

events.observed_evidence: The IEA released its September 2026 Oil Market Report on September 11. Reuters, citing the report, said the IEA now expects global oil supply to decline by 5.7 million barrels/day in 2026, versus roughly a 4% decline previously, as normal Gulf flows are delayed. The IEA also cut its 2026 Russian crude-production forecast by 125,000 barrels/day to 8.7 million barrels/day; August Russian crude output was estimated at 8.36 million barrels/day, down 200,000 barrels/day from July.
events.semantic_interpretation: This materially strengthens the persistence case for the energy shock. For Taiwan equities, the main negative channels are imported inflation, higher global yields, TWD pressure, freight/insurance costs and weaker non-AI global demand. Shipping-rate beneficiaries remain a partial offset, while energy-intensive and long-duration technology valuations face higher macro pressure.

events.observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 11 that Iran-aligned Houthi forces reached and captured strategic Perim Island and nearby Dhubab at the mouth of the Bab el-Mandeb shipping lane, after the prior capture of Mocha. Separately, Hormuz transits remained at seven vessels on September 10, far below pre-war traffic, while diplomatic efforts for a temporary Hormuz shipping arrangement were reported but not concluded.
events.semantic_interpretation: Control near Perim materially increases the probability of persistent Red Sea routing disruption at the same time Hormuz remains severely impaired. This is a dual-chokepoint global-trade risk rather than a single-route incident. For Taiwan, freight, insurance and imported-energy risks rise; container and bulk shipping earnings may benefit from rerouting and tighter vessel supply, but the broader equity impact is negative through inflation and discount rates.
